newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lonrho loses 6.5 pct in wake of Anglo deal.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho loses 6.5 pct in wake of Anglo deal.

text.p: Lonrho Plc lost 6.5 percent of its value on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Thursday in the wake of an announcement Anglo American Corp of South Afica had raised its stake in the group, dealers said.

"Lonrho ran right up when the deal was announced. Then a lot of overseas investors went long on the back of the deal after our market was closed. Basically they've come off now because they've realised there's not very much in it for them," a dealer said.
"I don't think the deal is bad, but I don't think it makes much difference to Lonrho shareholders," he added.
By 1147 GMT Lonrho shares were 80 cents lower at 11.50 rand. Almost 172,000 shares had traded.
Dealers said an end to selling was not in sight on the day and that the share could fall further.
Anglo on Tuesday bought former Lonrho chief executive Dieter Bock's remaining 18.3 percent stake for 180 pence per share.
This latest transaction raised Anglo's stake to a direct 25.9 percent and an indirect 2.2 percent.
Bock's predecessor Tiny Rowland on Wednesday sharply criticised the sale to Anglo. "It is fine for Anglo, but it's not fine for Lonrho shareholders," he said.
Lonrho shares in London were last at 149 pence per share.
